modelingNotes: Camp North End: Building 3, the Army Quartermaster warehouse on Woodward Avenue — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-cne-building-3.ts

The northernmost of the Quartermaster Corps' 1941–43 warehouses, Building No. 3 in the depot's numbering, between Hercules South (`clt-cne-hercules-south.ts`) and Woodward Avenue. One storey, 367 × 58 m (1,200 × 180 ft), steel-framed, its brick now mostly covered in metal siding; a low-pitched dark roof cut into five by firewalls, with one long raised monitor along its ridge, east to west. The working south face has concrete loading platforms under a canopy the full length, facing the Big Roof and Hercules South across the old rail yard; the west end on Statesville Avenue has a row of truck doors under a metal canopy; low annexes stand along the north side.
Identity: the long, low, dark-roofed shed with its single ridge monitor running end to end, paired with Hercules South's red-ribbed white roof.

Evidence: - OSM: the outline way/494906712 (height 8) and its parts way/835823918 and way/835823920 (the roof's two halves, 7.2), way/835823919 (the monitor, 10.1, gabled), way/835823921–835823926 (north annexes, 6). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016, 1 m (measured, NAVD88): ground 220.4–220.6 at the west end (the lowest; y = 0 is 220.5), 220.8 on the south, 221.5–221.7 at the east end; eaves 228.5 (8.0 m), the roof rising to 229.0 (8.5 m) at the monitor; the monitor y −10.4…9.3, its top 231.5 at the edges to 231.8 on the ridge (11.0–11.3 m); the south canopy 227.0 (6.5 m) over a platform at 222.0 (1.5 m); the west canopy 227.1 (6.6 m); a lean-to at the east end 225.1–225.8 (4.9 m); the north annexes 226.2 (5.7 m). - Charlotte-Mecklenburg Historic Landmarks Commission survey and research report (2017, landmarkscommission.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Ford-Motor-Co-Plant-SR.pdf), Building No. 3 (published): 180 × 1,200 ft, "about 27 feet high, with an east-west running monitor roof that raises its height about 7 additional feet", "in early photographs appears to be brick faced—today aluminum or vinyl siding covers much of the building's exterior"; the south face "contains concrete loading platforms sheltered by broad eaves that run the full length of the building", with many of the original loading doors; and "the western face ... is plain, but is characterized by 8 bays of overhead tractor-trailer loading doors, which are shaded by a rectangular metal canopy" (the report heads that sentence "Building No. 1", but it sits in the Building No. 3 section and Building No. 1's west face is the Ford front, so it is read as this building's). - Mecklenburg County tax parcel 07903101 (CAMP LANDOWNER LP): built 1943, modular metal and face brick. - USGS NAIP orthophoto (public domain): the dark charcoal roof, the monitor's edges, four transverse firewalls dividing the roof into five equal lengths (about 73 m), a sliver of pale grey-blue siding on the west wall.

No licensed photo of the building was found (Commons, Openverse, Mapillary — Mapillary has no imagery on Woodward or Statesville Avenue here). So: - the siding colour is the NAIP sliver, estimated; the roof's charcoal is from NAIP, pulled light; - the monitor's glazing (a clerestory band on both long faces) is assumed, as is its grouping; - door positions (south one per 12.2 m, west eight) are spaced evenly: the survey gives the west count only; - the firewalls' height (0.6 m over the roof) is estimated from their NAIP shadows.

Doubt: Joyfield Rise, 141 apartments on 5.3 acres "at the intersection of Woodward and Statesville Avenues", broke ground in August 2026 (Standard Communities); its site may take the west end of this building. Check OSM and current aerials before release.
Frame: the Ford plant's grid, as in `clt-cne-hercules-south.ts`; placement bearing 6.3. The origin is the outline's centroid, lng −80.8333358, lat 35.2488851.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-cne-building-3", model "clt-cne-building-3"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-cne-building-3.ts. Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
